Inspect and Recode Selected Person–Item Pairs

visualSubsetRecode.Rd

Interactively review flagged responses and recode selected cells. Use prepareSubsetInfo to prepare individual and class incident reports, or provide a manually constructed selection table.

Usage

visualSubsetRecode(dat = NULL, subsetInfo = NULL, ID = "ID", toRecodeVal = -91,
                   useGroups = NULL, positions = FALSE, comments = FALSE,
                   state = NULL, checkpoint = NULL)

Arguments

dat

Data frame of responses in wide format, with unique, nonmissing IDs. Required for a new review; omit when resuming through state.

subsetInfo

A data frame with columns named by ID and datCols. Each row selects exactly one person–item pair. Optional columns provide review groups, positions and comments. Alternatively, the result of prepareSubsetInfo.

ID

Person identifier column name; defaults to "ID", or the stored ID column for a prepared selection if this argument is omitted.

toRecodeVal

Single nonmissing replacement value, e.g. -91 or "mci". A character replacement can convert numeric response columns to character. Factor columns retain their class, adding the replacement level if necessary.

useGroups

Optional column identifying review subsets. With NULL, review one person at a time. For prepared selections, omission selects "issueId", so each incident is reviewed separately.

positions

Show blockPosition and subunitBlockPosition, and offer block-position selection. Both columns must contain positive whole numbers. For prepared selections, enabled automatically if all positions are available.

comments

Show the comment column. Missing comments are allowed. Enabled automatically for prepared selections.

state

A subsetReviewState object from a previous result's $state, or the path to an RDS checkpoint containing such an object. When resuming, omit dat, subsetInfo, and all recoding/display settings: the state retains the original inputs and settings.

checkpoint

Optional RDS file for automatic saving. Its parent directory must exist. A new review refuses to overwrite an existing file. When state is a file path, that file is also used as the checkpoint unless a different checkpoint path is supplied. An object supplied through state does not enable disk saving by itself.

Details

Only the selected person–item pairs are displayed and modified, including when people in the same review group have different selected items. Persons with the same item layout are displayed together. Missing response values are counted in the summary and retained by all recoding actions.

Options include recoding all selected nonmissing values, recoding only original values -99, -98, -97, -96, choosing block positions, leaving the current selection unchanged, flagging for later review, going back, resetting, pausing, and exiting. The non-valid-code filter uses the original input values, so revisiting a subset does not change which cells qualify.

Each review subset owns its recoding selection. Choosing another recoding action replaces that subset's previous selection. Reset removes its selection and restores original values except where another subset still requires recoding. Neither a ‘no’ decision nor flagging overrides an earlier recoding; use reset to withdraw it. Overlapping selections are reported during review and apply the same toRecodeVal once per cell. There is no person-versus-class precedence.

Unknown IDs or item columns and missing required identifiers cause errors before review. Optional metadata containing NA does not remove rows. Unlike earlier versions, invalid required inputs are rejected rather than omitted. Numeric person IDs are matched and displayed without losing precision; their original type is preserved in the returned response data. A standard R menu cancellation offers an exit; declining exit returns to the same subset. Both ‘pause review (resume later)’ and confirmed exit return a resumable state. Selecting ‘yes’ at the final end confirmation marks the review complete. Cancelling that confirmation pauses at the confirmation itself. Resuming a completed state returns the completed result without opening menus.

Pausing and resuming. The state retains the original response data, complete selection table, settings, review order and position, decision history, and active cell selection for every review subset. Returned response data are reconstructed from these original data and selections, so original-code filters, reset and overlapping incidents behave the same after resuming. Resume with visualSubsetRecode(state = result$state) or visualSubsetRecode(state = "review.rds"). Do not start a new review using already modified responses if the intention is to continue the previous review.

With checkpoint, the initial state and each completed decision or navigation change are saved before continuing. The file contains the state itself, not the full result list. Writes use a temporary file in the same directory and replace the previous checkpoint only after serialization succeeds. A changed or stale checkpoint is rejected instead of overwritten. Use one active reviewer per checkpoint file.

An R interrupt, such as Ctrl+C, returns completed work with status = "interrupted"; the assigned result contains its resumable state. Interrupts are deferred while committing a decision and its checkpoint. An unfinished block submenu has no effect and is repeated after resuming. If R is forcibly terminated, resume from the latest successfully written checkpoint; an in-memory result alone does not survive termination of R.

An ordinary error during review raises a condition of class subsetReviewError, with the last committed state in condition$state. For example, a failed checkpoint write leaves the previous checkpoint and the previous accepted decisions intact; the failing decision must be repeated after the file problem is resolved. Invalid, incomplete or unsupported state formats are rejected before reviewing. Automatic revisiting of flagged entries and different replacement values per incident are not implemented.

Value

A named list with dat, the modified data frame; subsetInfo, the reviewed selection rows joined to the decision history; state, a versioned subsetReviewState object; and status, one of "paused", "interrupted", or "completed". Positional access via [[1]] and [[2]] is retained. If an interrupt arrives after completion has already been committed, the result remains "completed".

The history includes choice, timeStamp (UTC), and list columns selectedCells and selectedBlocks. selectedCells records the incident's active selection after that decision; selectedBlocks records positions chosen in that decision's block submenu (empty for other actions). These snapshots may be repeated when joined to multiple source selection rows. The unjoined entries are also retained in state$history as group, choice, timeStamp, selected_cells, and selected_blocks. Repeated reviews produce multiple history entries; this is not a final-status or final cell-difference table. Unreviewed entries are absent from the history but remain in the state. An exit before any decision returns unchanged data, empty history, and the full resumable state.

The state also retains original_dat, subset_info, settings, groups, index, phase ("review" or "finish"), selections, and completed, together with a format version, session_id, and revision. Treat the state as an opaque object: save and pass it back unchanged, rather than editing its fields.

See also

prepareSubsetInfo, vignette("subset_review", package = "eatPrep")

Author

Karoline Sachse

Examples

dat <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), I1 = c(1, 0), I2 = c(0, 1))
issues <- data.frame(issueId = "V1", level = "person", targetId = "P1",
                      scope = "item", target = "I1", comment = "Display error")
info <- prepareSubsetInfo(dat, issues)
summary(info)
#>   issueId  level targetId persons items cells overlappingCells
#> 1      V1 person       P1       1     1     1                0
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- visualSubsetRecode(dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci",
                             checkpoint = "review.rds")
# Select "pause review (resume later)" or interrupt with Ctrl+C.
result$status
result <- visualSubsetRecode(state = "review.rds")

# Without automatic disk saving, an assigned result can be resumed in memory.
result <- visualSubsetRecode(dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
result <- visualSubsetRecode(state = result$state)

# Manually constructed selections remain supported.
selection <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), datCols = c("I1", "I2"), group = "G")
result <- visualSubsetRecode(dat, selection, useGroups = "group")
} # }
